why: The C reader over the `.nros_boot_config` blob: validates magic + version + the `NROS_BOOT_SET_NODE_NAME` bit and returns a pointer into the baked `char[64]`, or NULL. The generated C entry passes it as the `session_name` to `rclc_support_init_named`, which is what fixed the PID-derived session name (#98). The governing constraint is RFC-0045's: a device is never told anything at startup. There is no argv to parse, no environment to read and (on the embedded targets) no filesystem to load a YAML from, so the identity a desktop node gets from `ros2 run --ros-args -r __node:=talker` has to be BAKED into the image at link time. rcl/rclc/rclcpp/rclrs have no counterpart to any of this for the same reason they have no counterpart to a linker script. OUR LANGUAGES DISAGREE, and this is the row to act on: the blob defines FOUR fields and the C side reads exactly one. There is no `nros_boot_config_locator`, `_domain_id` or `_namespace`, and the C/C++ emitter that WRITES the blob (`emit_boot_config_static`, nros-cli-core/src/codegen/entry/mod.rs:236) hardcodes `.domain_id = 0`, `.locator = ""`, `.namespace_ = ""` and never sets their bits -- a C image gets its locator and domain from the `NROS_ENTRY_LOCATOR` / `NROS_ENTRY_DOMAIN_ID` compile definitions instead, which is the second delivery path RFC-0045 was written to remove. Rust's `BootConfig::from_baked` reads all four. Consequence: RFC-0045's follow-on `nros config patch` tool would patch three fields no C image reads, and the parity between the languages that the shared blob was supposed to buy is one field deep.
